name: Gemuendina
description: Broad rhenanid with a leading mouth, paired anterior eyes, small mosaic armour and a long finless tail; tail-driven swimming with restrained pectoral trim.

sources.title: Johanson and Smith (2005), Origin and evolution of gnathostome dentitions
Südkamp (2021), Ikonen des Hunsrückschiefers, illustrated specimens pp.17–18
Westoll (1967), Radotina and other tesserate fishes

notes: A finless tapering tail follows the illustrated specimen account; generic shark dorsal/caudal fins, fin spokes, ventral gill rows and sting are omitted.
Living thickness, soft-tissue cavity, exact denticle/tessera arrangement, fin flexibility, pigmentation and motions are explicit reconstruction choices.
0.30 m is a representative reconstructed length close to the illustrated 304 mm specimen, not a claimed species maximum.
All action names are compatibility labels for specimen gestures; no Devonian gameplay rules are prescribed.

V3 living mass and regional pigmentation follow user art direction as explicit interpretations; accepted clay-02 volume is retained except for the documented continuous orbital integration correction.
Seven sequential axial tail segments provide locomotor waves; limited pectoral-edge motion steers and trims the body.
V4 user-directed face refinement moves the oral recess and paired eyes to the leading front. Accepted V3 posterior silhouette and regional pigmentation retained; living orientation is interpretive.

Paired anterior eyes above the leading mouth follow the user reference direction; dorsal eye-like motifs are skin markings, not additional eyes. This living orientation is an artistic reconstruction rather than a fossil certainty.
